title: basel-problem-oq-01-oq-01-oq-02

problemStatement.plain: Can Apéry's proof of $\zeta(3)$ irrationality be formalized in Lean? The proof uses an explicit combinatorial identity for the approximation sequences; formalizing it would require significant Mathlib infrastructure around hypergeometric functions and WZ-theory.

currentState.focus: Prove Apéry recurrence and growth estimates
currentState.nextAction: Read problem.md thoroughly and acquire full context.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Added Apéry a-sequence, harmonic numbers, lcm infrastructure, linear form definition. File now 350 lines, 20 theorems, 9 defs, 6 sorries (up from 4 — added Nair bound and denominator control). Critical path dependencies now clear.
builtItems: Defined aperyB: ℕ → ℕ (Apéry number sequence)
Proved aperyB_zero, aperyB_one, aperyB_two, aperyB_three (initial values)
Defined aperyA: ℕ → ℚ (a-sequence via recurrence)
insights: Apéry numbers bₙ = ∑ C(n,k)²C(n+k,k)² computable as ℕ in Lean via Finset.sum
Initial values verified by norm_num: b₀=1, b₁=5, b₂=73, b₃=1445
No WZ-theory in Mathlib; recurrence must be proved by direct manipulation or auxiliary lemma
The decay rate (√2-1)⁴ ≈ 0.029 < e⁻³ ≈ 0.050 is what makes the proof work — denominator growth is only e³ⁿ
Can bypass prime number theorem for lcm bound using Nair (1982): lcm(1,...,n) ≤ 4^n
a-sequence satisfies same recurrence as b-sequence with a₀=0, a₁=6
lcm bound lcm(1,...,n) ≤ 4^n (Nair 1982) bypasses PNT for denominator control
Critical path: recurrence → growth → decay + denominator control → irrationality
Harmonic numbers H_n and generalized H_n^{(s)} needed for a-sequence closed form
nextSteps: Prove aperyB_recurrence by combinatorial identity expansion
Define the a-sequence with harmonic number coefficients
Prove growth bound from recurrence by induction
Submit Aristotle companion for routine lemmas
